correctness.rationale: The shell-integration derivation supplies the exact quartic for every compact convex planar base. The independently recomputed symbolic discriminant equals 8*q^2*G(q)/27. An exact rational proof of a 10^-18 pi enclosure and sixteen Bernstein signs on four rational intervals certifies G strictly decreases across 0<=q<=1; opposite endpoint signs force one simple threshold. Four distinct negative roots exist for small q by two explicit limiting quadratics; root continuity/discriminant signs give four real below, two real above, and one ordinary double at the boundary. Positive coefficients exclude nonnegative real roots. Regular polygon inequalities have separate rational certificates. Actual included verify.py was executed successfully.

value.rationale: The equal Cartesian square is a canonical four-dimensional construction. Unlike the planar base, whose Steiner quadratic always has two real roots, its square exhibits a sharp, geometry-independent transition between all four roots real and only two real. This yields a complete isoperimetric classification over a continuum of nonsmooth or smooth convex bases and the non-obvious sharp regular-pentagon/hexagon cutoff. It is not just a coefficient computation; strict discriminant monotonicity and the full root-type continuation are essential.
